column1: # Curated help for the keys worth explaining. Hand-written, and deliberately NOT
# produced by gen-schema.py: that file is regenerated from a device and would
# overwrite anything written here. Merged with it by name, in the browser.
# The rows for keys in settings.tsv describe what the odi-oss image does with
# them. The rest describe the stock firmware -- /etc/runomci.sh for how a key
# reaches omci_app, and measurement for the rest -- and are shown only in the
# read-only stock-keys view. Where a claim is not grounded it says so rather
# depends  KEY=VALUE, joined by &. When unmet the UI says the key is ignored,
#          because that is what the firmware does with it.

column3: help

Becomes `omci_app -t`. Anything outside the listed values falls back to bridge. Switching between HGU and SFU also needs a CS factory reset — this key alone leaves a stale WAN entry behind and the ONU keeps running as a router.

Bitmask, DECIMAL -- `flash set` accepts nothing else. Passed as `omci_app -cr`. Each bit loads one plugin from lib/features; the field below decodes it. Bit 0x4 is `ignore_conn_uniNode_check`, which suppresses the ME 171 uniNode association check; the stock firmware ships with 4. On the 2024 firmware that same bit also skips populating the resolved association, which stops the ONU forwarding at all.
Bitmask, DECIMAL. Passed as `omci_app -cb`. Each bit loads one plugin from lib/features; the field below decodes it against this image.

Bitmask, DECIMAL. Passed as `omci_app -cme`. Bit 0x100 is `cf_apply_customized_veip_slot_id`, which is what makes OMCI_VEIP_SLOT_ID take effect at all -- set the slot id without this bit and nothing happens.
Bitmask, DECIMAL. Passed as `omci_app -cmc`. Each bit loads one plugin from lib/features; the field below decodes it.
1 starts omci_app with `-m enable_wq`.
Answers OK to OMCI operations the stack cannot actually satisfy. Some OLTs refuse to finish provisioning without it.
Read by boa, configd, led, mib and xmlconfig — and NOT by omci_app or checkomci. It does not affect provisioning, which was confirmed from the binaries rather than assumed.

Passed to omci_app, and read as a single byte -- so the MSB of the entity id you want, 14 for 0x0e01, not the whole id. It does nothing on its own: bit 0x100 of OMCI_CUSTOM_ME loads `cf_apply_customized_veip_slot_id`, and without that bit the value is ignored. 255 is the default here; whether the OLT ends up bridged to the VEIP or the physical UNI is what it provisioned on ME 47, not this key alone, unless OMCI_CUSTOM_ME bit 0x100 is set.

Handed to the europa driver at boot by insert_europa.sh, and read by runsdk.sh to choose which stack starts. This key is not only yours: with PON detection on, pondetect rewrites it and reboots after about 24 seconds of light without PON sync, so a value that changed on its own came from there.
The first four characters of the serial number, and must match it.
32 hex characters.
1 is the shipped value.
The device login for SSH and telnet. Not this UI's password, which lives in /etc/config/confd.auth.
The device login for SSH and telnet.

The VLAN untagged frames are placed in on the host-side switch port. Upstream issue #475 reports setting this to 0 as the fix for an ONU that registers but forwards nothing; the shipped values are confirmed to forward correctly on their own, so this is recorded as untried rather than recommended.
As above, for the second switch port.
Whether the resolver addresses below are used or taken from the upstream connection.
column4: 0=0 — from upstream|1=1 — use the addresses below

column3: Writes the decoded OMCI conversation with the OLT. 2 is the parsed form, landing in /tmp/omcilog.par — about 95 KB for a full registration. Reading that exchange is the only way to see what the OLT is actually asking for.
Which message types to log. 4294967295 logs everything.
Leave at 0. /tmp is an unbounded RAM disk on a device with about 1.5 MB free, so the debug level can exhaust memory; parsed message logging is bounded and is what you actually want.
column4: 0=0 — errors only|1=1 — errors|2=2 — warnings|3=3 — info|4=4 — debug (can exhaust memory)

column3: What `pondetect` does with the PON MAC, every two seconds. On: if the SerDes sees light but never achieves sync for about 24 seconds, it concludes the PON type is wrong, rewrites PON_MODE to the other one and hard-reboots -- so a stick that comes back as EPON after a fibre fault did that to itself. Off does not stop pondetect: it still resets the SerDes CDR on every unsynced sample, it just never touches the flash. Detection is skipped entirely while GPON_SN is the factory default RTKG11111111. Read at boot by runsdk.sh, so a change needs a reboot.
column4: 0=0 — off (CDR reset only, never rewrites PON_MODE)|1=1 — on (may rewrite PON_MODE and reboot)

column3: Never writable here. Like the SerDes mode, getting it wrong can take the link down and with it every way into the device.
The address SSH, this UI and the exporter answer on. Saving moves it at once, and this page with it: note the new address first, or turn on the second address below as a way back.
Netmask for the management address, applied with it.
A second, fixed address beside the first (br0:2), for reaching the stick when the first is changed to something you cannot route to.
Only used when the second address is on. 192.168.100.1 is the common choice.
1 lets the manual VLAN below reach the services; any other value means no manual tag at all, whatever the VLAN ID says.
Only read when VLAN config mode is 1. Mode 1 tags with the VLAN ID and priority below; any other value is no manual tag.
column4: 0=0 — off|1=1 — tag using the VLAN ID below

column3: The C-VLAN omcid adds upstream and removes downstream on the services the OLT provisions: your ISP service VLAN. Used only when VLAN config mode is 1 AND manual VLAN mode is 1, and only with a priority set too.
802.1p priority bits carried in the tag. Same gating as the VLAN ID; an empty priority means no manual tag, as on the stock firmware.
What the OLT authenticates. Four-character vendor prefix followed by eight hex digits. Lose it and the ONU will not come up on the line.
Stored as the hex of an ASCII string, shown decoded above. Many OLTs authenticate on the serial number alone and leave this empty; others require it.
The MAC of eth0, its host port and br0.
The logical ONU id a CTC-profile OLT asks for. Left unset when the OLT does not require one. Cannot be cleared from here: the store refuses an empty value.
The password that goes with the LOID.
The value omcid actually answers when it differs from LOID. Saving LOID writes this too.
As above, for the password.
What the OLT is told image 0 runs (software image entity, 14 characters at most).
What the OLT is told image 1 runs.
The equipment id the OLT reads in ONU2-G (20 characters at most). The stock firmware reports IGD.
ONU2-G OMCC version, decimal. 128 (0x80) is what this image and the stock firmware report.
ONU2-G vendor product code, decimal. 15 is what this image and the stock firmware report.

Free-text `host:port` of a remote syslog collector, read by this image, not the stock firmware. Empty (the shipped default) leaves remote logging off. Once wired into settings.tsv this is a SERVICE RESTART key -- the syslog forwarder restarts to pick up the new address, the fibre service stays up, no reboot needed -- but that apply path is not implemented yet, so saving this key here does nothing until it lands.

Free-text `host` or `host:port` for the odi-oss NTP client, read by this image, not the stock firmware. Passed to busybox `ntpd -p`, which resolves the string with the shared host2sockaddr/str2sockaddr helper -- a bare host defaults to port 123, and a trailing `:port` overrides it. Empty (the shipped default) leaves the NTP client off. Once wired into settings.tsv this is a SERVICE RESTART key -- the NTP client restarts to pick up the new server, the fibre service stays up, no reboot needed -- but that apply path is not implemented yet, so saving this key here does nothing until it lands.
